name: Trollkarl Bonchar

related.relation: the beast below the road he sought

facts.text: Trollkarl Bonchar is a level-65 named with 30,000 health. Calm, he looks like a Valkyn sorcerer; when attacked he becomes 'The Rift' and stays so while he has aggro.
As the Rift he calls a morkenhet out every 10-20 seconds and casts Rift Strike (300).

Allakhazam lists Trollkarl Bonchar, The Rift, Rift and Bonchar's Shade in Trollheim. A May 2003 raid said the morkenhet were the real fight and that killing the Rift gave nothing; a 2003 visitor asked if killing it brings back the morvalt at the desk.
Swedish and Old Norse trollkarl means sorcerer, wizard.
facts.source: Swedish and Old Norse glossaries (to verify the period sense)

story:
Bonchar was a trollkarl, a sorcerer, of the people the Troll Fathers tamed. He was one of the first Valkyn born after the taming, and he was the cleverest of them, and the Fathers taught him more than they taught the others: the old words, the deep roads, the shape of the dark under the city. When the morvalt broke into Trollheim he did not flee with the rest of his people to Midgard. He stayed in the upper city, hiding among his savage cousins, wearing their paint, waiting.

He was looking for the way the Fathers had gone. They had gone down, everyone knew that, below the holy halls and below the mound, by a road only they knew. Bonchar believed the road was not a tunnel at all. He believed the Fathers had gone through the dark itself, through a place where the dark is thin, and he spent years in a chamber of the middle city listening for it. He found it. He opened it. He meant to follow them through.

Instead the rift came through him. Now he stands in his chamber with a sorcerer's face and a sorcerer's patience, very still, as if listening, until someone touches him. Then he is not Bonchar any more. His face splits and the dark behind it opens, and the thing in his place is the Rift itself, a great tear of nothing that strikes at whoever is near, and the morkenhet, the darkness-things, crawl out of it one after another, every ten or twenty breaths, for as long as anyone fights him. The morvalt who kept watch over his chamber vanished when the Rift first opened; players of old asked whether killing it would bring them back. It does not.

When the fight ends, he is Bonchar again, standing still, listening. The Allakhazam scholars recorded his shade in the same halls. The Valkyn say he does not remember. They say that if he ever does, he will finish opening the door, and then everyone will know where the Fathers went.
legend: The Rift isn't hard, the morkenhet are. One or two groups on add patrol with stuns and area damage, everyone else on the Rift; healers at the base of the stone with aggro magnets near them for the adds that get through. Target the Rift with nearest-enemy, it's easy to lose. Don't drag him past his tether or he walks home and resets. The first known kill on Kay in May 2003 dropped nothing and gave no experience, and they killed him anyway. These days the Rift's helm and leggings drop. Pac healers' area stuns and supp spiritmasters on add patrol are the classic answer.

loremasterTopic.text: A trollkarl, a sorcerer, who stayed in Trollheim when the morvalt came and went looking for the way the Fathers had gone. He found where the dark is thin and opened it. It opened him instead.

bookPage: From the notes of Hallveig, the Valkyn guide. My grandmother knew Bonchar when he was young. She said he was the cleverest of all of us, and the saddest, because he was the only one the Fathers loved enough to teach the deep words. When they left he could not bear it. He said he would follow them, wherever they had gone. She told him the Fathers had left us so that we would have to stand on our own. He said that was a story for children. She said she did not know which of them had been right. She said she still did not know.
